# Hydrogen Water for Blood Sugar Support: What New Research Shows

Hydrogen water may help support healthy blood sugar levels, though results for insulin resistance were mixed in a recent clinical trial.

## What the Research Shows

A new study tested hydrogen-rich water in 50 people with [Type 2 Diabetes](/explore-by-condition/type-2-diabetes). The [original research study](/study/electrolyzed-hydrogen-rich-water-for-oxidative-stress-suppression-and-improvement-of-insulin-resistance-a-multicenter-prospective-double-blind-randomized-control-trial-1775650467165) found that drinking hydrogen water did not significantly improve insulin resistance compared to regular filtered water. However, it did lower blood lactate levels, which may benefit people with diabetes and [Metabolic Syndrome](/explore-by-condition/metabolic-syndrome).

This was a high-quality study. It was double-blind, meaning neither patients nor doctors knew who got hydrogen water or regular water. The trial lasted 12 weeks and included multiple medical centers.

## How Hydrogen Water Delivery Works

Molecular hydrogen (H2) can be delivered through drinking hydrogen-rich water. This water is made by special machines called water ionizers and hydrogen water generators. Companies like Echo Water™ make these devices for home use.

The study used electrolyzed hydrogen-rich water. This is water that has been processed to add dissolved hydrogen gas. The hydrogen acts as an antioxidant in your body. It may help reduce harmful molecules called free radicals.

## How to Apply This Research

Based on the study protocol, participants drank hydrogen water for 12 weeks. While the study didn't specify exact amounts, most hydrogen water research uses about 1-2 glasses per day.

Here's how you might incorporate hydrogen water:

**Daily Amount**: Start with 1-2 glasses (8-16 ounces) of hydrogen water daily
**Timing**: Drink it with meals or between meals
**Consistency**: Use it regularly for at least 8-12 weeks to see potential benefits
**Monitoring**: Track how you feel and any changes in energy levels

Remember, this study focused on people with diabetes. If you have [Insulin Resistance](/explore-by-condition/insulin-resistance) or blood sugar concerns, work with your doctor to monitor your levels.

## What to Look For in Hydrogen Water Machines

Not all hydrogen water is the same. Quality matters for getting potential health benefits.

**Dissolved Hydrogen Levels**: Look for machines that produce water with at least 1.0 ppm (parts per million) of dissolved hydrogen. Higher levels may be better.

**ORP Levels**: Good hydrogen water should have a negative ORP (oxidation-reduction potential). This measures the water's antioxidant power.

**Third-Party Testing**: Choose machines that have been tested by independent labs. This confirms the hydrogen levels are accurate.

**Fresh Production**: Hydrogen gas escapes quickly from water. Make and drink hydrogen water fresh for best results.

## Understanding the Mixed Results

This study adds to the growing body of [hydrogen whole body research](/blog/category/whole-body). While insulin resistance didn't improve significantly, the reduction in blood lactate levels is interesting.

High lactate levels can be a problem for people with diabetes. When your body can't use glucose properly, it may produce more lactate. Lower lactate levels might mean your body is handling energy better.

The researchers noted that hydrogen water was safe. No one had serious side effects during the 12-week study.

## Key Takeaways

• **Hydrogen water is safe** for people with Type 2 diabetes based on this 12-week study
• **Blood lactate levels improved**, which may benefit overall metabolism
• **Insulin resistance didn't change significantly**, so don't expect major blood sugar improvements
• **Quality matters** - look for machines that produce at least 1.0 ppm dissolved hydrogen
• **Consistency is key** - the study lasted 12 weeks with daily use

## What This Means for You

Hydrogen water might be a helpful addition to your health routine, but it's not a cure for diabetes or insulin resistance. The lactate reduction could support better energy metabolism. However, more research is needed to understand all the effects.

For more studies on hydrogen therapy, check our [hydrogen research database](/proxy/) to see the latest findings.

**Important**: Consult your healthcare provider before starting any new health regimen, especially if you have diabetes or other health conditions.
